chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abdul Kareem ibn Amr, from Zurara, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), that he said:
The one who cannot find (afford) a sacrificial animal (hady) and wishes to bring forward the three days (of fasting) during the first ten (days of Dhu al-Hijjah), so there is no problem.

key_terms.أَوَّلِ الْعَشْرِ: The first ten (days of Dhu al-Hijjah)
key_terms.فَلَا بَأْسَ: There is no problem / It is permissible
key_terms.هَدْيًا: Sacrificial animal offered by the pilgrim
key_terms.يُقَدِّمَ: To bring forward (an act of worship to an earlier time)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a pilgrim who cannot afford the sacrificial animal during Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi outlines the concession (rukhsa) for a Mu'tamir performing Tamattu' who lacks the means for the sacrificial animal, allowing them to substitute the required fasting with three days observed during the first ten days of Dhu al-Hijjah. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic principle of easing religious obligations based on financial capacity, ensuring the pilgrim fulfills their duty without undue hardship. It reflects the practical application of divine mercy in Hajj rituals, prioritizing the completion of the act over strict adherence to the specific timing of the sacrifice.

en.hubeali:
Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, from Abdul Kareem Bin Amro, from Zurara, 
(It has been narrated) from one of the two (5<sup>th</sup> or 6<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘
The one who cannot find a sacrificial animal and would like to bring forward the three days (of Fasting) during the first ten (days), so there is no problem’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn abu Nasr has narrated from ‘Abd al-Karim ibn ‘Amr from Zurarah who has said the following: “One of the two Imam, (abu Ja’far or abu ‘Abd Allah), ‘Alayhim al-Salam, has said, ‘
One who cannot find an offering and likes to fast the three days during the first ten days, it is not an offense for him to do so.”
